configurationChanges.text: No configuration schema changes. Every configuration kind keeps schema version 1. Published releases, signed pack bytes, workflow pins and drafts are not read, rewritten or republished by this upgrade.

operationalActions.text: Take and verify a backup with the version that is running now (platform 1.0.0), in maintenance mode, immediately before the upgrade, so that rollback loses nothing.
Deploy the platform 1.1.0 files without admitting users, then run the pre-flight from them. Read every blocker and warning; a warning needs the owner's explicit acceptance.
Rehearse the upgrade on a restored copy of the backup and keep the rehearsal evidence before upgrading the real installation.
Run the upgrade with the privileged migration account, in maintenance mode. After it validates, maintenance mode is released by the upgrade itself.
Prove rollback by restoring the pre-upgrade backup into a clean database and keep the rollback evidence.

compatibilityWarnings.text: A backup made by platform 1.0.0 restores into platform 1.1.0 with the migrations still pending (restore applies none). Run the upgrade on the restored copy to bring it current.
The upgrade adds one table (the migration record) to the operations schema, with row-level security. It changes no existing table, row, audit event, configuration release, pack or document.

steps: Stop the platform 1.1.0 application and keep the installation in maintenance mode.
Restore the verified pre-upgrade backup into a clean database and a clean document and package area.
Deploy platform 1.0.0 (the build that made the backup) against the restored database. Never start an older application against the upgraded database.
Run the installation validation, then release maintenance mode.
rollback.dataLossStatement: Rolling back discards everything created after the pre-upgrade backup, including anything done after the upgrade finished. It cannot be recovered from the backup.
